ruxen 0.2.2: nginx 1.30's upstream defaults, `charset` and `add_header_inherit`, logs and lifecycle as nginx keeps them, systemd readiness and watchdog, and a batch of compatibility fixes. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio, epoll where `io_uring` is blocked), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

**Upstream connections follow nginx 1.29.7's defaults** (#582): HTTP/1.1 to the upstream, and `keepalive 32 local` for every `upstream {}` block unless it says `keepalive 0;`. The pool is one queue per upstream, as nginx's keepalive cache. One deliberate difference: over HTTP/1.1 with no pool (`keepalive 0;`, or `proxy_pass` to an address with no `upstream {}` block), ruxen still sends `Connection: close`, so the backend closes first and the proxy doesn't collect TIME_WAIT sockets. Under load, nginx 1.30.6 filled its ephemeral ports there and ran at 8.8% of 1.24.

## Performance

**HTTP/2 streams cost about half the instructions** (#699). Each stream runs in a task of its own, and its 11 KB future was copied about five times on the way into it. Under callgrind those copies were 56k of the 99k instructions of an h2c `return 200` request. It is boxed now. Against 0.2.2's main without the change: `h2c_hello` +7.4%, `h2_tls_hello` +6.7%, `h2c_static_8k` +2.1% (i7, 6 ABBA pairs each).

## Security

ruxen has no known production users yet; these were found comparing with nginx 1.30.6 and by review, and fixed in the open. Upgrade from 0.2.1.

- **A server chosen by SNI used the default server's `ssl_protocols`** (#586): a vhost's own `ssl_protocols` had no effect. Each server with its own certificates now has its own protocol versions, as nginx 1.29.2+ selects the server before the version is negotiated.
- **rustls-webpki 0.103.16** (RUSTSEC-2026-0382): earlier versions may accept certificate paths through the distrusted emSign intermediates (#476). The release workflow's new daily advisory check found it.
- **Request framing as nginx 1.30 has it:**
  - method tokens are `A`-`Z`, `_` and `-` only (#485);
  - a second `Proxy-Authorization` is a 400 (#590);
  - so is a second `host` next to HTTP/2's `:authority` (#609);
  - at most `max_headers` (1000) header lines (#584);
  - a bare LF in an upstream's chunked response is refused (#585).
- `X509_verify_cert`'s return value is checked as well as its error (#517). There is no known bypass: AWS-LC sets an error on every failure today.

## Fixes

- **A response that doesn't need the request body no longer waits for it** (#627). For `return`, static files and their error pages, nginx answers at once and drops the rest of the body, and on HTTP/2 resets the stream with NO_ERROR. ruxen read the whole body first, so a slow or stopped client got no answer until `client_body_timeout`. An `index` or `error_page` that leads to `proxy_pass` still reads it. A body refused as too large that an `error_page` sends upstream goes there empty, instead of the client's `Content-Length` with no bytes, which left the upstream waiting.
- **`proxy_send_timeout` is the time between two writes** to the upstream (#490), not a limit on the whole request: a large body to a slow but steady upstream no longer gets a 504.
- **A `rewrite` without a flag searches the locations again** once the location's rewrite directives are done (#682), as nginx does. Before, the request stayed in the first location and was served from it. `proxy_pass` with a URI part now applies its substitution after such a rewrite. A `break` now stops before a location's `return`, which then doesn't answer, as in nginx (#697).
- **Logs:**
  - each `access_log` and `error_log` file is opened once and shared through descriptors (#523, #648). Before, every `error_log` line opened, wrote and closed the file on the worker thread, and an `error_log` FIFO hung the worker;
  - SIGUSR1 reopens each log on its own (#522);
  - the root helper reopens the log files a reload added (#498);
  - buffered access logs no longer keep memory per reload (#528).
- **Reloads and shutdown:**
  - a reload that waits on a blocked open no longer keeps SIGTERM waiting (#497);
  - a failed reload frees what it prepared (#499);
  - a reload whose new `io_uring` rings don't fit `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` runs those workers on epoll instead of failing (#635);
  - SIGTERM leaves without exit handlers while the workers still run (#525);
  - the root helper is forked from one thread only (#527);
  - a panicking cache manager pass doesn't end the zone's upkeep (#524);
  - upstream TLS caches no longer keep every version of a changed CA, CRL or client certificate (#500).
- `client_body_in_file_only` writes a file for an empty framed body too (#628).
- **`proxy_limit_rate` paces a body that comes at once** (#700). The bytes of the last read went out unpaced, and so did up to 64 KiB that arrived with the head: a 40 KB body at 20000 B/s took under a millisecond. It now takes 2 s (nginx: 1.8 s). Each read is capped at what the rate allows, as nginx's event pipe does, so a low rate sends about a second's worth at a time. A chunked body read whole is paced too, and an answer `proxy_intercept_errors` hands to an `error_page` isn't (nginx doesn't read it).

## nginx compatibility

- **`proxy_cookie_domain`, `proxy_cookie_path` and `proxy_cookie_flags`** (#40): the `Domain`, `Path`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite` of the upstream's `Set-Cookie` rewritten as nginx does, the same output header for header, on 101s and on the cookies an X-Accel-Redirect carries too. Named captures (`(?<name>…)`) now work in the replacements of these and of `proxy_redirect`. `proxy_cookie_flags` was refused at startup until now, so that the flags it sets wouldn't be dropped silently.
- **`charset` and `charset_types`** (#464): `; charset=…` on `Content-Type` for the types in `charset_types` (text/html always), on static files, `return`, error pages and proxied responses without one, as nginx's charset filter. Nothing is converted: `source_charset`, `override_charset` and `charset_map` stay without effect, which `--compat` reports. h5bp's `nginx.conf` loads now.
- **`add_header_inherit` and `add_trailer_inherit`** (nginx 1.29.3, #598): `merge` keeps the inherited headers under a level's own, the fix for the location whose one `add_header` dropped the server's security headers; `off` inherits nothing.
- **`return` takes the response type from `types` / `default_type`** (#691), as nginx: with the usual `default_type application/octet-stream;`, `return 200 "ok";` is an octet-stream there, and ruxen said `text/plain`.
- **Times are local** (#614): `$time_local`, `$time_iso8601` and error-log times are in the local time zone, not UTC.
- **The error log says what nginx says:**
  - a request refused while its head is read: `client sent invalid method`, `invalid header line: "…"`, `duplicate header line`, `invalid host header`, … (#663);
  - a head that never completes: `client timed out`, `client prematurely closed connection`, logged with 408/400 in the access log (#509);
  - TLS handshake and read errors at `info` (#595);
  - the workers' lifecycle: `start worker process`, `gracefully shutting down`, `exit`, `worker process N exited with code 0` (#669). nginx-tests waits for the last one after a reload;
  - every signal with its sender's pid, and `exit` (#518).
- **Variables:** `$request_id` (#487) and `$pid` (#559). `$http_x_foo` finds an `x_foo` header (#624).
- **Configuration:**
  - `listen` takes `*:port`, a host without a port and a host name (#654);
  - the same address twice in one server is refused (#564);
  - so is `set` on a read-only built-in variable such as `$uri` (#574);
  - `ssl_object_cache_inheritable`, `ssl_certificate_cache` and `ssl_certificate_compression` (#601);
  - `proxy_limit_rate` takes variables, read once the upstream's header is in, so `$upstream_http_*` can set the rate (nginx 1.27.0, #601);
  - `-v` (#475);
  - `Content-Length` from an upstream is at most 2^63 - 1, as nginx's `ngx_atoof` takes it.
- **TLS:** of two `ssl_certificate` of one key type in a server, the last is served, as nginx's OpenSSL keeps it (#670).
- **Proxy:**
  - `Content-Length` upstream follows the client's body framing (#493);
  - the upstream path is escaped only for a quoted or internal request (#575);
  - an `error_page` that leads to `proxy_pass` keeps the error's status (#675);
  - a request under `limit_conn` whose client closes gives its count back at once, not 100–200 ms later (#705);
  - a `proxy_pass` in one `if` stays the handler when a later matching `if` has none; without an upstream that's nginx's 500 `no upstream configuration` (#703).
- **HTTP/2:** `large_client_header_buffers` bounds each field and the header list, with GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (#623). Where the h2 crate follows RFC 9113 and nginx doesn't, ruxen keeps the RFC behaviour, now documented (#347).
- **An `alias` after a rewrite maps nothing**, as nginx 1.30 refuses it (#589).
- **`gzip_disable msie6` and `keepalive_disable msie6 | safari`** test the `User-Agent` as nginx does (#477): an Opera that says MSIE 6 isn't MSIE 6, IE 6 with SV1 keeps its POST connections, and Chrome or Firefox on a Mac isn't Safari. Ranges adding up to more than 2^63 - 1 bytes are a 416. The new `range` and `gzip_negotiation` fuzz targets found these.

## Operations

- **systemd** (#502): `Type=notify` readiness (`READY=1` once every listener is bound and root dropped, `RELOADING=1` around reloads), and a watchdog that pings only while every worker makes progress. The shipped unit uses both.
- **Packaging:** the tarballs, images and crate carry a `NOTICE` with nginx's licence for `mime.types` and the other material taken from nginx (#479).
- **Supply chain** (#480): each tarball has a CycloneDX SBOM next to it and build-provenance and SBOM attestations (`gh attestation verify ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz -R gvozdetsky/ruxen`). The binaries carry their crate list (`cargo audit bin`), and the image an SBOM.
- **CI** checks dependencies against the RustSec advisory database daily (#476), and fuzzes five more parsers on every pull request: `range`, `gzip_negotiation`, `http_date`, `basic_auth` and `h2_frames` (#477). rustls-pemfile, unmaintained, is gone.
- The nginx-tests harness answers as nginx/1.30.6 (#617), and its runner no longer counts a log with binary bytes as 0/0. `clippy` gates CI (#152). The config corpus reports how many configurations load with nothing that behaves differently from nginx (#478).

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.2.2-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.2.2/ruxen-v0.2.2-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.2.2-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.2.2-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

Container image, amd64 and arm64:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/gvozdetsky/ruxen:0.2.2
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

It runs as an unprivileged user. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`, so under it ruxen runs on epoll; [`contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.2/contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json) allows `io_uring` and nothing else beyond the default (`--security-opt seccomp=contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`). On a host with many cores, the container's memlock limit may need raising for `io_uring` (`--ulimit memlock=134217728`, #612); without it the workers that don't fit run on epoll (#635). A hardened systemd unit and a logrotate snippet are in [`contrib/`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/tree/v0.2.2/contrib).

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

## Tests

nginx-tests: 182 of the 197 files that apply pass (0.2.1: 172 of 192), see [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.2/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md). Config corpus: ruxen loads 218 of 238 real-world configurations (92%; 0.2.1: 217), 171 of them with nothing that behaves differently from nginx (#478).
